lesson.title: Kubernetes from Zero, part 17: scheduling basics
lesson.description: Steer Pods onto the right nodes with nodeSelector and node affinity, keep replicas apart or together, and spread them evenly across zones.
lesson.tested: Every command ran on a four-node kind v0.33.0 cluster (node v1.37.0, kubectl v1.37.2) on 10 Nov 2026
lesson.rule: Label your nodes, then say where Pods must or should go. Use topology spread to survive a zone loss, and read FailedScheduling events when a Pod waits.

cheatsheet.intro: Where Pods land, how to steer them, and the commands from Lesson 17.

rows.name: Filtering
rows.role: Removes every node where the Pod cannot run: not enough CPU or memory, a taint it does not tolerate, or a required label the node does not have. Survivors are feasible.

rows.name: Scoring
rows.role: Ranks feasible nodes using spreading, your preferences and how full each node is. The top-ranked node's name is written into spec.nodeName.

rows.name: FailedScheduling
rows.role: The event the scheduler records when no node survives filtering. The message is a count per reason. The scheduler keeps retrying.

rows.name: nodeSelector
rows.role: A map of labels the node must have, all of them. The simplest hard rule.

rows.name: Required node affinity
rows.role: A hard rule with operators such as In, NotIn, Exists and DoesNotExist. No matching node, no scheduling.

rows.name: Preferred node affinity
rows.role: A soft rule. weight is 1 to 100. The scheduler adds the weights of the preferences a node matches to its score.

rows.name: Pod anti-affinity
rows.role: Do not put me in the same place as Pods with a given label. topologyKey decides the place (hostname = one node, zone = one zone). The required form caps replicas at the number of domains.

rows.name: Topology spread
rows.role: Keep matching Pods even across domains. maxSkew is the largest allowed difference. DoNotSchedule keeps a Pod Pending if placing it would break maxSkew; ScheduleAnyway still places it.

items.what: The scheduler filters out nodes where a Pod cannot run, scores the rest, and binds the Pod to the top-ranked one.
Required pod affinity on the zone key placed the workers on the same node as cache, worker2.
After uncordon, the nine shop replicas settled at 3/3/3.
Read FailedScheduling. The cordoned spread case said 2 node(s) didn't match pod topology spread constraints.

commands.note: one Pod per node when required

homework.intro: Create the four-node kind cluster from the lesson (kind-multinode.yaml, name k8s-multi) and the namespace k8s-from-zero. Lab output uses the prefix k8s-ep16. Answers are in the separate answer key.

sections.title: Recall
sections.hint: Answer from memory, then check the lesson.

exercises.q: What are the scheduler's two steps, and what happens if no node survives filtering?
exercises.a: Filtering finds feasible nodes; scoring ranks them and the scheduler writes the top-ranked node into spec.nodeName. If no node survives, the Pod stays Pending and the scheduler records a FailedScheduling event as a count per reason. It keeps retrying, so fixing the label or rule is enough.

exercises.q: What is the difference between required and preferred node affinity, and what does IgnoredDuringExecution mean?
exercises.a: requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution is a hard rule: no matching node, no scheduling. preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution is a soft rule with a weight from 1 to 100. IgnoredDuringExecution means the rule is only checked at scheduling time; if someone removes a label later, Pods already running there stay.

exercises.q: What do maxSkew and whenUnsatisfiable mean on a topology spread constraint?
exercises.a: maxSkew is the largest allowed difference between the domain with the most matching Pods and the one with the fewest. DoNotSchedule keeps the Pod Pending if placing it would break maxSkew. ScheduleAnyway places it and prefers the nodes that keep skew lowest. Spread constraints do not move running Pods later.

exercises.q: Apply pod-ssd.yaml and pod-gpu.yaml. Where did each Pod land, and what did the FailedScheduling message for needs-gpu say until you labeled worker3 gpu=true?
exercises.a: fast-disk ran on the node labeled disktype=ssd (k8s-ep16-worker2). needs-gpu stayed Pending: 0/4 nodes are available, 1 had an untolerated taint, 3 didn't match the node affinity/selector. After kubectl label node ... gpu=true, the scheduler retried on its own and needs-gpu ran on that node. No reapply was needed.

exercises.q: Apply the api Deployment with a hard zone rule and a weight-80 preference for ssd. Where did the four replicas land, and what trap does the lesson point out?
exercises.a: All four landed on the ssd node in the allowed zone (k8s-ep16-worker2). The hard rule ruled out zone-c. The weight of 80 for ssd outscored everything else. A strong preference can pile every replica onto one node.

exercises.q: With maxSkew 1, six shop replicas, then cordon zone-c and scale to nine, what counts did the lesson record, and why did a ninth Pod stay Pending?
exercises.a: Six replicas landed 2, 2 and 2. After the cordon and scale, the counts were 3, 3 and 2, plus one Pending Pod with no node. A ninth Pod in zone-a or zone-b would make 4 against zone-c's 2, a skew of 2. Events listed an unschedulable node, an untolerated taint, and topology spread constraints. After uncordon the counts became 3, 3 and 3.

sections.title: Predict the outcome
sections.hint: Write your prediction first. Then check the answer key.

exercises.q: You scale a Deployment with required pod anti-affinity on kubernetes.io/hostname from 3 to 4, and you have three workers. What happens?
exercises.a: The fourth replica stays Pending. Required anti-affinity is a strict promise: with three nodes, the fourth replica has nowhere to go. The FailedScheduling message says nodes didn't match pod anti-affinity rules. Use the preferred form, or a spread constraint with maxSkew 1, if you want spread when you can.

exercises.q: A Pod stays Pending and you suspect a typo in a node label. What does the lesson tell you to compare?
exercises.a: Labels are case-sensitive: disktype: SSD does not match ssd. Compare the Pod's rule with kubectl get nodes -L disktype, and read the FailedScheduling event with kubectl describe pod.

exercises.q: Your spread constraint seems to ignore some nodes. What cause does the lesson name?
exercises.a: Nodes without the topologyKey label do not count as a domain. Label every node.
